ESTIMATE: a coarse monthly calendar per latitude zone from the basin's known climate, to verify with CHIRPS monthly rainfall and gauge records. The basin straddles the equator: one rainy season north of about 2 N (roughly April to October), one south of about 2 S (roughly October/November to April), and two rainier peaks with no real dry season in between (March to May, September to November). Rivers run low when their catchment's dry season has drained them: northern rivers (Ubangi, Uele) about February to April, southern ones (Kasai, Lualaba, Luapula) about August to October.
sources: Washington, R. et al. (2013) Congo Basin rainfall climatology: can we believe the climate models? Phil. Trans. R. Soc. B 368: 20120296
Alsdorf, D. et al. (2016) Opportunities for hydrologic research in the Congo Basin. Reviews of Geophysics 54: 378-409
